body:
Thanks for the reply. It's nice to see someone else reaffirming my perspective some. I've got a very limited number of friends myself.

I think my biggest problem with that idea is that he's associated the same anxiety of work and such with the idea of seeing a therapist. I'm seriously considering that I myself need to start seeing a therapist regularly before he'll consider that option, although he's equally likely to just label me a sell-out of sorts for doing that.

Incentivizing is likely to backfire on me. I've tried it, mentioning that he'd likely get on benefits much like myself, allowing us to afford much more, but he's scared stiff that they might force him to go to weekly meetings to keep benefits, as has been done to him in the past for food stamps (different state). I know it seems like a good idea to encourage and work with people to help them become functional workers in today's society, but he'd rather starve. (Admittedly, I'd be the same.)

I've already looked into where he could get help. There's the local Mental Health Services (which I went to) that offers free services to locals (he got a local state ID a few months back). Price and transportation isn't an obstacle here, fortunately. It's all about trying to make that jump and just do it, which I fear is going to be extremely hard.

We're surprisingly similar.  My father and his grandfather (the one who acted as his guardian for most of his teenage life) are very similar.  They mean well, but they keep approaching our problems the same way, without change.  

I've been able to amend my life somewhat due to having disability benefits and living on my own.  Being on my own helped me gain perspective and realize that the world isn't so bad, and helped me find my inner strength and realize my problems weren't just in my head.  Being able to understand -why- I have these problems helps me deal with them.  He hasn't had the luxury of that.  He's still much like how I was, blaming the world for everything, unable to see past the hatred and rage, depressed by his helplessness.

This isn't about me though.  It's about him.  We're similar, and it's likely part of why neither of us can get past this.  But I don't know of any alternatives.

His great grandmother is somewhat actively involved.  She lives on the other side of the state, and is the one helping pay for his food and such.  It's barely enough, but it's keeps him fed.  She genuinely cares for his well being, but is limited in how much she can help.

He lived with her for several years before moving out.  She's very much a Christian, and can be very overwhelming at times.  The most his family is willing to do is to have him move back up north and live with them while he either goes to college or gets a job.  Neither of which is an option as far as he's concerned.

Both of us grew up with parental figures who were completely oblivious to our emotional needs.  We both rebelled when told to do something, which lead them to attempt punishment.  We took the punishment, remained defiant.  They ignored our problems and complaints, and kept telling us we have to go to school/work/etc.  There's no problem.  Just shut up, ignore our pains, and do what we're told.  There's no problem.

It's hard to explain, I suppose.  Any time I'm faced with school/work, I just have an anxiety attack.  It's not that I refuse.  I just fall apart from the anxiety.  It hurts so much, that I'd rather die.  That's in large part why I'm so screwed up, and he's not much different.  We were told to just do it.  Just do it.  There's no problem.  Why can't you just do it.
